title: Sep 17 Results + Sep 18 Preview: Five Wins, Solid Pitching Reads
summary: 5-4 on Sep 17 with strong road favorites. Reds top the Sep 18 slate.

content.value:
## Sep 17 Recap: The Favorites Delivered

From a pitcher's perspective, yesterday was about reading matchups correctly when it mattered. We went 5-4 on the day, and the wins came where they should've—with our higher-confidence plays. The misses? All coin flips under 52%. That's baseball.

## Breaking Down the Board

The Astros, Rays, Padres, White Sox, and Angels all came through—notice a pattern? Every single winner was at 61% or higher. When you've got conviction backed by pitching matchups and bullpen depth, trust it. The four losses were all tight calls, basically toss-ups where we had minimal edge.

That Brewers-Pirates miss stung a bit at 52%, but when you're that close to even money, you're really just making an educated guess. The Mets and Tigers picks at 50-51%? Those are the ones that keep you humble on the mound.

## The Pitching Lesson

Here's what I saw: when we had a clear pitching advantage combined with home field or better bullpen depth, we cashed. The Astros at home, the Rays with their defense, the Padres in Coors with the better arms—these weren't lucky guesses. These were reads based on who controls the strike zone and who doesn't.

The close calls went sideways because that's what happens when two evenly-matched staffs face off. No shame in that.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Cubs @ Reds

Looking ahead to Sep 18, I'm zeroing in on Cincinnati at home against the Cubs. Clay Holmes gets the ball for Chicago—he's been serviceable but nothing special. Chase Burns takes the mound for the Reds, and from a pitcher's eye, he's got better stuff right now.

This is a 50% call, which means it's tight, but Great American Ball Park favors the home team when the starter can locate. Burns has shown he can work both sides of the plate, and the Reds bullpen has been getting outs late.

## The Bottom Line

Sep 17 was solid—not spectacular, but profitable if you stuck with the higher-confidence plays. Sep 18 looks tighter across the board, but I like what the Reds bring to the table at home. Sometimes you've got to trust your eyes on the pitching matchup, even when the numbers say it's a toss-up.

Stay sharp out there.
